title: 2008 HMMT February Guts Problem 16
statement: Point \(A\) lies at \((0,4)\) and point \(B\) lies at \((3,8)\). Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the point \(X\) on the \(x\)-axis maximizing \(\angle A X B\).

solutions.text: \(\quad 5 \sqrt{2}-3\) Let \(X\) be a point on the \(x\)-axis and let \(\theta=\angle A X B\). We can easily see that the circle with diameter \(A B\) does not meet the \(x\)-axis, so \(\theta \leq \pi\). Thus, maximizing \(\theta\) is equivalent to maximizing \(\sin \theta\). By the Law of Sines, this in turn is equivalent to minimizing the circumradius of triangle \(A B X\). This will occur when the circumcircle of \(A B X\) is the smaller of the two circles through \(A\) and \(B\) tangent to the \(x\)-axis. So let \(X\) now be this point of tangency. Extend line \(A B\) to meet the \(x\)-axis at \(C=(-3,0)\); by Power of a Point \(C X^{2}=C A \cdot C B=50\) so \(C X=5 \sqrt{2}\). Clearly \(X\) has larger \(x\)-coordinate than \(C\), so the \(x\)-coordinate of \(X\) is \(5 \sqrt{2}-3\).
